issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for PersonService.deletePerson: the problem statement (DELETE /persons/{personId}) and the template/service expect deletePerson to take a UUID personId (deletePerson(UUID personId)), but the solution's PersonService implements deletePerson(Person person) while the solution's PersonResource invokes personService.deletePerson(personId) passing a UUID. This inconsistency breaks the intended REST contract and will cause a compilation error because the called method signature does not exist in the solution's service.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the deletePerson API consistent: change the solution's PersonService.deletePerson to accept a UUID (personId) to match the template and REST endpoint. Example: public void deletePerson(UUID personId) { this.persons.removeIf(person -> person.getId().equals(personId)); } and keep PersonResource calling personService.deletePerson(personId). This preserves the DELETE /persons/{personId} contract and resolves the compilation error.

issues.description: The concept is deleting a Person by its identifier. The problem statement describes the DELETE endpoint as DELETE /persons/{personId} (personId: UUID). In the template PersonService the method is declared as deletePerson(UUID personId). In the solution, PersonResource calls personService.deletePerson(personId) (passing a UUID) but the solution's PersonService declares deletePerson(Person person) (accepting a Person). This inconsistent identifier/type for the same conceptual operation (delete by UUID) will confuse students and leads to a compilation/mapping mismatch: the REST resource expects a service method taking a UUID, while the service implementation in the solution expects a Person object.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the deletePerson API consistent across artifacts. Restore or add a service method with signature deletePerson(UUID personId) in PersonService (matching the problem statement and template) and implement it to remove persons by id (e.g. persons.removeIf(p -> p.getId().equals(personId))). Alternatively, add an overloaded deletePerson(UUID personId) that delegates to the existing Person-based method. Ensure PersonResource invokes the service method with the same parameter type (UUID) so compilation and conceptual mapping are consistent.
